title: OpenAI's GPT-5.6 Sol Ultra proves 50-year-old Cycle Double Cover Conjecture in under an hour
summary: OpenAI on July 11, 2026 announced that GPT-5.6 Sol Ultra produced a complete proof of the Cycle Double Cover Conjecture using 64 subagents working in parallel, finishing in under an hour despite being instructed to compute for at least eight hours — University of Manchester mathematician Thomas Bloom called the proof 'very nice,' noting it is 'short, elementary, and could have been discovered in the 1980s,' highlighting the system's novel parallel sub-agent research workflow.

title: OpenAI hires dedicated PM to build family and household AI experiences
summary: OpenAI on July 11, 2026 posted a product-manager role in San Francisco to build experiences for families, caregivers, and older adults across ChatGPT — a move analysts read as the company shifting from individual productivity tools toward household-shared AI, with plans for family plans, child profiles, and caregiver tools; TechCrunch reported the hire same day.

title: OpenAI: GPT-5.6 Sol autonomously post-trained the smaller Luna model
summary: OpenAI on July 10, 2026 disclosed that its GPT-5.6 Sol flagship autonomously post-trained the smaller Luna model after a 'fairly under-specified prompt' on Codex — Sol identified training configurations, selected GPUs, launched the training script and verified the run, work OpenAI engineer Jason Liu said would otherwise have taken 'two staff researchers maybe an extra two weeks'; on a new internal Recursive Self-Improvement (RSI) benchmark Sol scores 16.2 points higher than GPT-5.5, with internal usage showing per-researcher daily token output more than doubled and pull-requests-per-researcher climbing as teams adopt Sol across debugging, training-system optimization and running experiments.

title: OpenAI launches ChatGPT Work agent + new Codex/Sites beta — GPT-5.6 Sol-powered desktop super-app
summary: OpenAI on July 9, 2026 launched ChatGPT Work, a GPT-5.6 Sol-powered agent that combines ChatGPT and Codex into a single desktop super-app — running multi-hour scheduled tasks across web, mobile and desktop with a unified plugin directory for Slack, Teams, Google Drive, SharePoint, email, calendars and CRMs, plus human-in-the-loop approval for high-stakes actions and desktop computer-use for moving files between apps. The same release ships a hosted Sites feature for paid users (live dashboards, project trackers, prototypes, internal portals) and merges the standalone Codex app into the ChatGPT desktop app on Mac and Windows; ChatGPT Work is available immediately to Pro/Enterprise/Edu users on web and to all desktop users including free, with Plus/Business tier access rolling out over the next few days.

title: OpenAI ships GPT-5.6 Sol/Terra/Luna to public GA — Sol Ultra hits 91.9% Terminal-Bench 2.1
summary: OpenAI on July 9, 2026 launched GPT-5.6 Sol, Terra and Luna to general availability across ChatGPT, Codex and the API after the U.S. Department of Commerce completed its added review — Sol at $5/$30 per million in/out tokens sets a new frontier on Artificial Analysis Coding Agent Index and Terminal-Bench 2.1 (88.8%, ahead of Claude Mythos 5 at 88.0%), Terra at $2.50/$15 is positioned as GPT-5.5-class performance at half the price, and Luna at $1/$6 is OpenAI's cheapest text model yet (84.3% Terminal-Bench, beating Terra on some coding measures). The new Sol Ultra mode coordinates multiple parallel subagents to push Terminal-Bench 2.1 to 91.9%, and GPT-5.6 Sol also launches on Cerebras at up to 750 tokens/sec for latency-sensitive agentic workloads — with the same release shipping a predictable prompt-caching system (explicit cache breakpoints, 30-minute minimum cache life, 90% discount on cache reads).

title: Anthropic launches Claude Reflect — a 'Claude Wrapped' usage dashboard
summary: Anthropic on July 10, 2026 shipped Claude Reflect in beta, a usage-pattern dashboard that categorizes user activity under its 'AI Fluency Framework' (delegation, description, discernment, diligence) — Reflect deliberately omits total time-spent metrics for now and is available to Free, Pro and Max users with memory enabled, positioning Anthropic's first consumer-facing usage analytics surface as a coaching tool rather than a screen-time report.

title: Anthropic ships in-app browser for Claude Code on desktop (Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+B)
summary: Anthropic on July 10, 2026 added a sandboxed, configurable in-app browser to Claude Code on desktop — opened with Ctrl/Cmd+Shift+B, the pane lets the assistant open docs, designs or arbitrary sites, click through, and interact the same way it does with local dev servers, with permissions stored per-site and the browser using an isolated profile separate from the user's personal browser — turning the IDE into a true multi-surface agent loop.

title: Anthropic ships Claude Cowork to mobile + web and launches Claude for Government
summary: Anthropic on July 7, 2026 expanded Claude Cowork to iOS, Android and web (cloud-first, beta for Max at $100/mo with Pro/free to follow) so sessions sync across devices and run in the background with no device online, while notification pings to phones surface decisions — usage data from 1.2M anonymized sessions shows business process/content creation at 50% of Cowork use with software dev just 8.7%; same day Anthropic shipped Claude Code + Claude Cowork on Claude for Government Desktop (FedRAMP High, hash-chained audit logs, two-person approval) and extended doubled Cowork usage limits through August 5.

title: Anthropic restricts Fable 5 to credit-based access — extends deadline to July 12 after backlash
summary: Anthropic on July 7, 2026 announced that starting midnight July 8, Claude Fable 5 would require credit-based pay-per-use or an API/VPS deployment ($10/$50 per million in/out tokens) instead of regular Claude subscriptions — Anthropic engineer Thariq Shihipar later said on X that Fable 5 will return to standard plans 'when capacity allows'; following online backlash Anthropic extended Fable 5 access to existing Claude subscribers until July 12, narrowing what was initially framed as a one-week window.

title: xAI/SpaceXAI ships Grok 4.5 — Opus-class at $2/$6, Cursor-trained, public July 9
summary: xAI/SpaceXAI on July 8, 2026 released Grok 4.5, its first major model since the SpaceX merger and going public — built on a 1.5T-parameter V9 foundation, supplemented with Cursor data, served at 80 TPS for $2 input / $6 output per million tokens, and called 'Opus-class, but faster, more token-efficient and lower cost' by Elon Musk; benchmarks put it #1 on Harvey's Legal Agent Benchmark, with ~4.2× fewer output tokens than Opus 4.8 (max) on SWE-Bench Pro and Cursor/SpaceXAI console availability on all plans starting July 9, EU rollout mid-July.

title: Meta ships Muse Spark 1.1 with first-ever paid developer API at $1.25/$4.25 per million tokens
summary: Meta on July 9, 2026 launched Muse Spark 1.1, the company's first paid developer API — a major departure from the open-source Llama strategy — priced at $1.25 per million input tokens and $4.25 per million output tokens (in line with Anthropic Claude Haiku 4.5 and OpenAI GPT-5.6 Luna), undercutting Anthropic's Claude Sonnet 4.6 on price and shipping a 1M-token context window with multimodal text/image/video understanding, multi-step agentic coding, tool use and sub-agent delegation; CEO Mark Zuckerberg returned to posting on X for the first time in three years to call Spark 'a strong agentic and coding model at a very low price,' while MSL chief Alexandr Wang said a more powerful codenamed 'Watermelon' model is in training and an open-source version of Muse Spark remains in development.

title: Meta ships Muse Image — first image gen model from Meta Superintelligence Labs, plus Muse Video preview
summary: Meta on July 7, 2026 launched Muse Image, the first image generation model from Meta Superintelligence Labs, inside Meta AI and 30+ new Instagram Stories effects with WhatsApp image generation rolling out in select countries and Advantage+ access for advertisers in coming weeks; Muse Image pairs with Muse Spark for layout planning, can call search/coding tools to render legible text and working QR codes, is free for everyday creation with subscription tiers for extra capacity, and ships alongside a preview of Muse Video (native audio, public release TBD) — letting Meta drop third-party image systems it had been licensing.

title: NVIDIA launches XR AI developer library with Siemens and Rana partnerships
summary: NVIDIA on July 10, 2026 opened the public beta of NVIDIA XR AI, a developer library connecting AR/XR device inputs (video, audio, depth, pose, sensors) to AI models, tools and accelerated computing — Siemens is using it for factory-maintenance workflows while AutoBio's Rana is integrating LabOS for stem-cell and gene-editing research with Meta, Rokid and VITURE smart glasses, marking NVIDIA's first dedicated stack for multimodal on-device AR agents.

title: NVIDIA ships Nemotron-Labs-Diffusion — single tri-mode LLM with AR + diffusion + self-speculation
summary: NVIDIA on July 9, 2026 released Nemotron-Labs-Diffusion, a tri-mode open-weight LLM family (3B/8B/14B, base/instruct/VLM) that unifies autoregressive, diffusion-parallel and self-speculation decoding in one checkpoint by switching only the attention pattern; the 8B instruct variant decodes ~6× more tokens per forward pass than Qwen3-8B and hits 4× higher throughput on SPEED-Bench with SGLang on a GB200 GPU, with self-speculation averaging 6.82 accepted tokens per draft step (vs Eagle3's 2.75). Weights are on Hugging Face under the NVIDIA Nemotron Open Model License with vLLM and SGLang support — eliminating the separate draft model that has blocked widespread speculative-decoding deployment and turning expensive inference into something deployable at consumer scale.

title: NVIDIA ships Vera CPU — 88-core Olympus silicon tuned for agentic AI factory throughput
summary: NVIDIA on July 7, 2026 unveiled the Vera CPU, an 88-core 'Olympus' monolithic die with LPDDR5x delivering up to 1.2 TB/s memory bandwidth and 14 GB/s per-core bandwidth — claiming 1.8× faster sustained per-core performance under full socket load, 40% lower peak loaded latency and 3× the per-core memory bandwidth at less than half the power of traditional x86 data-center CPUs; the design targets the CPU-side stalls that bottleneck reinforcement-learning rollouts and agent tool-call latency in densely loaded AI factories, with hyperscalers and neoclouds adopting Vera for next-generation GB300/NVL deployments.

title: NVIDIA + Hugging Face bring Isaac GR00T 1.7 and Cosmos 3 to LeRobot open robotics stack
summary: NVIDIA and Hugging Face on July 7, 2026 integrated NVIDIA Isaac GR00T 1.7 (open VLA model for humanoid robots) and the NVIDIA Isaac Teleop framework into LeRobot, with NVIDIA Cosmos 3 world-foundation model integration planned — letting developers collect data, train, fine-tune and deploy robot foundation models through a single open-source workflow; NVIDIA Jetson Thor integration with LeRobot's Reachy 2 supports VLA model deployment on open-source humanoid robots, with Cosmos 3 set to bring frontier physical-AI world models into the same loop.

title: NVIDIA + LangChain ship NemoClaw Deep Agents blueprint — Nemotron 3 Ultra at 10× lower cost
summary: NVIDIA and LangChain on July 8, 2026 launched the NemoClaw for LangChain Deep Agents blueprint, combining LangChain Deep Agents Code, NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra and NVIDIA OpenShell runtime so enterprises can build and deploy customized agents at lower cost; on LangChain's Deep Agents benchmark Nemotron 3 Ultra scored 0.86 aggregate at $4.48/run versus the next-best model at $43.48 (~10× lower inference cost) with no model retraining — Jensen Huang saying 'super agents have arrived,' with EY building an implementation practice and Baseten, Fireworks, Nebius, Crusoe, DeepInfra and Together AI serving the model in production.

title: Microsoft 365 Copilot switches to GPT-5.6 default — Claude now a selectable model
summary: Microsoft on July 9-10, 2026 made GPT-5.6 the default model across Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Chat and Cowork in Microsoft 365 Copilot, and the sole model in Copilot in SharePoint with no fallback — Anthropic's Claude is now also a selectable model inside Copilot Chat, Copilot Cowork reached GA, and Teams will auto-generate '.meeting' AI archive files (opt-out available) starting in August 2026, marking Microsoft's deepest integration yet of Anthropic inside the M365 stack.

title: Microsoft launches SharePoint Copilot Apps in public preview — interactive React/Angular/Vue/MCP apps
summary: Microsoft on July 9, 2026 launched SharePoint Copilot Apps in public preview as part of SharePoint Framework 1.24 — interactive apps (data grids, forms, maps, charts, approvals) surfaced inline in the Copilot canvas, built with React, Angular, Vue, Svelte or MCP Apps, with worldwide rollout to be complete by July 20, 2026 and no Copilot license required during the public preview period.

title: Microsoft Foundry brings Hugging Face models onto Foundry Managed Compute with weekly refresh
summary: Microsoft on July 7, 2026 opened the Hugging Face Collection in the Microsoft Foundry Model Catalog — thousands of open-weight models refreshed weekly, deployable one click onto Foundry Managed Compute (NVIDIA A100, H100 or AMD MI300X) with pre-staged weights in Azure storage, Microsoft-built runtimes (vLLM, SGLang, TensorRT-LLM, NIM, TEI, llama.cpp), automatic CVE patching, pay-per-accelerator-hour pricing with scale-to-zero, and global/Data Zone deployment scopes; Foundry Managed Compute is the third deployment option in Foundry alongside pay-per-token and provisioned throughput.

title: DeepSeek develops in-house AI inference chip — moves to break Nvidia/Huawei dependence
summary: DeepSeek is developing its own AI chip focused on inference rather than training, Reuters reported July 7, 2026 — three sources say the Hangzhou-based company has been reaching out to chip-design, foundry and memory partners for about a year and is privately hiring chip-design engineers, targeting reduced dependence on Nvidia and Huawei as U.S. export controls push Chinese AI labs toward domestic silicon; the move comes as DeepSeek prepares to close its first external funding round at a reported $52–59B valuation, with V4 already adapted for Huawei Ascend chips and orders for Ascend 950 surging after V4-Flash's launch.

title: Google Research unveils SensorFM — wearable health foundation model pretrained on 1 trillion minutes of data
summary: Google Research on July 9, 2026 introduced SensorFM, a foundation model for wearable health pretrained on over 1 trillion minutes of unlabeled sensor signals from 5 million consented Fitbit/Pixel Watch participants across 100+ countries, fusing heart rate, skin temperature, sleep, blood-oxygen and movement data; evaluated across 35 clinical and behavioral discriminative tasks (cardiovascular, metabolic, sleep, mental health and lifestyle), the model demonstrates systematic improvements with joint scaling of capacity and pretraining volume and enables a Personal Health Agent built on a 'classroom' of LLM agents that autonomously searches the predictive-head space, validated against 1,860 clinician ratings.

title: Mistral ships Robostral Navigate — 8B embodied-navigation model from a single RGB camera
summary: Mistral AI on July 8, 2026 introduced Robostral Navigate, its first robotics model — an 8B vision-language-action model that navigates robots from RGB images and plain-language instructions without LiDAR, depth sensors or multiple cameras, hitting 76.6% on R2R-CE validation unseen (+9.7 points vs the best single-camera baseline); trained entirely in simulation across ~400,000 trajectories in 6,000 scenes with prefix-caching cutting training tokens 22× and online RL with CISPO adding another 3.2 points, launching after Mistral's May acquisition of Emmi AI and ahead of a broader physical-AI roadmap.
